Criterion: Verify that emergency oxygen is available for all occupants of the air vehicle. Standard: The emergency oxygen system(s) provides a supply of breathing gas to all crewmember and passengers in the event of an emergency where the flow of oxygen from the primary system is interrupted or stopped. It is desirable for the system to activate automatically and alert the crewmembers that it is activated. The duration of the supply is maximized to the greatest extent possible, and as a minimum, supplies enough oxygen to allow the crew and passengers to safely descend from the aircraft's maximum altitude to below 10,000 feet MSL. Method of Compliance: Emergency oxygen system capabilities are verified by inspection of drawings, demonstrations in mockups, and analysis of test data from system qualification tests. Emergency oxygen system operation to maximum aircraft altitude is verified by analysis of data from the oxygen system qualification program, including altitude chamber man rating tests. References: JSSG-2001: 3.3.10.2.2 JSSG-2010: 3.7, 4.7; 3.13, 4.13

Standard: Emergency oxygen is provisioned and accessible to crewmembers for protection against loss of pressurization, smoke and fumes, and ejection (if applicable). The emergency oxygen systems need to be accessible by users from their seated locations. The emergency oxygen supplies a minimum 94% oxygen concentration at a volume and pressure sufficient to ensure crewmember performance to descend from the air vehicle maximum ceiling to an altitude below 10,000 feet MSL. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Review FMECA to verify that all emergency oxygen systems are covered.
(2) Inspect component hardware configuration documents to confirm compliance with hardware drawings and location to crew stations. Analysis.
  (1) Verify Emergency Oxygen System Safety Analysis shows that failures across the system are annunciated and have automatic responses. Demonstration.
    (1) Demonstrate that crewmembers are able to access the emergency oxygen masks and don them within five seconds at each crew station. Test.
      (1) Lab test: Conduct testing with appropriate facial and mask hardware to ensure the functional performance of the emergency oxygen system allows crewmembers to perform all flight-critical tasks.
      (2) Lab test: Conduct testing of automated breathing system switching to verify uninterrupted transition to emergency system.
      (3) Lab test: Conduct testing to verify emergency oxygen subsystem performance is sufficient for descent from air vehicle ceiling to 10,000 feet MSL. Prior to entering operational test or operations, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
    (2) Conduct review of materials, connectors, wiring, and subsystem assemblies to ensure compatibility with the air vehicle.
